title: Prefetch risk & model safeguards — admission and rollback playbook
content:
Purpose:

This note collects pragmatic guidance for admitting speculative prefetch/decoding activity and for safe, auditable rollbacks when speculation misfires. It focuses on admission heuristics, a bounded speculation model, the integration contract with scheduler/kernel/KV layers, operator runbook steps, and the telemetry we need to make automated gating reliable.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: hosted + dedicated runtime; applies to all model variants we host.
- Intent: minimize customer-visible regressions while capturing upside from prefetching (reduced tail latency and higher throughput). Provide conservative, measurable default gates that teams can tune per workload.

Background / Motivation:
Many workloads benefit from being able to speculatively prefetch tokens (prefix reuse, kernel warm paths, KV priming). But the cost of incorrect speculation is non-trivial: wasted GPU cycles, KV pollution, and potential quality regressions. We need a small, well-instrumented surface to admit, contain, and if necessary, revert speculation with clear operator guidance.

High-level design principles:
- Bounded speculation: always cap token/compute budget per request.
- Deterministic admission: make decisions from measurable inputs (latency budget, kv hotness, model variant compatibility, uncertainty estimate).
- Observability-first: tag every speculative action and emit compact metrics for waste, rollback, and quality drift.
- Fast safe rollback: provide cheap ways to stop and recover when divergence or cost thresholds are hit.

Admission criteria (what the admission controller should check):
Inputs available to controller:
- request.model_id (string)
- request.sequence_length_estimate (int)
- request.latency_slo_ms (int)
- prefix_similarity_score (float 0..1)
- kv_hot_score (float 0..1) — heuristics for prefix presence
- kernel_profile.steady_state (bool) + kernel_preferred_variant (string)
- uncertainty_score (float) — per-request language model entropy / logprob proxy
- customer_tier (enum) — free / standard / premium

Example default heuristics (conservative starting point):
- Allow admission only if: 
  - latency_slo_ms >= 250 AND 
  - kv_hot_score >= 0.7 OR prefix_similarity_score >= 0.6 AND 
  - uncertainty_score <= 1.2 (low entropy) AND 
  - model variant is quantized-compatible with kernel_preferred_variant
- If customer_tier == free => do not admit unless kv_hot_score >= 0.9.
- Max speculative tokens per request = min(ceil(seq_len_estimate*0.25), 48).
- Per-node speculative compute budget throttles (%) to avoid global burst: default 8% of GPU time reserved for speculation.

Bounded speculation model (safety knobs):
- Token budget: absolute max tokens and time budget (e.g., 48 tokens or 60ms compute on a single GPU).
- Eviction policy: speculative KV entries are tagged with short TTL (e.g., 30s) and a spec_tag so they can be quickly evicted when waste rises.
- Fallback grace: if speculation fails, do not schedule more speculation for that client for X minutes (exponential backoff per-identity).

Integration contract (APIs & hooks):
1) Admission Controller API (sync)
- Input: request context (see inputs above)
- Output: admit boolean, max_tokens, hint_kernel_variant, spec_id (opaque)
- Side effect: increments per-route speculative counter with spec_id tag

2) Scheduler hooks
- prefetch_reserve(spec_id, tokens, ttl_ms): scheduler reserves bundle slots; returns reservation_id or error
- on_spec_finish(reservation_id, success:boolean, wasted_tokens:int) => releases reservation and records waste

3) KV-cache hooks
- kv.reserve_key(key, spec_tag, ttl)
- kv.commit_key(key, spec_tag) — mark promoted (longer TTL)
- kv.invalidate_tag(spec_tag) — bulk drop speculative entries on rollback

4) Kernel probe API
- kernel.can_fastpath(model_variant, seq_len) => bool
- kernel.register_probe_result(spec_id, latency_ms, model_mismatch_score)

5) Telemetry/tracing
- Attach spec_id to traces. Tag spans: speculative.prefetch, speculative.kv_insert, speculative.kernel_warmup

Rollback strategies (ordered by cost and speed):
1) Soft-abort + graceful retry: stop speculative emission, invalidate speculative KV entries, re-run inference on baseline variant (cheap).
2) Variant fallback: if kernel mismatch detected, switch to compatible kernel variant and re-decode. If prefetch was irreversible, treat as partial waste and emit rollback metric.
3) Prefix rewind + re-decode: roll the decoder state back to prefix boundary and re-decode from there (expensive but deterministic).
4) Live patch: if only a handful of speculative tokens conflict, apply token-level patch/overwrite in the streaming layer (requires strict contract about token boundaries).

Operator / oncall playbook (short):
- Alert triggers: speculative.rollback_rate > 1% of admissions for 10m AND speculative.wasted_tokens_rate rising > 30%
- Immediate actions:
  1. Move routing for affected model to conservative mode: disable admission controller (force admit=false) for the route.
  2. Run kv.invalidate_tag(recent_spec_tag_prefix) if KV pollution suspected.
  3. If kernel mismatch suspected, flip traffic to kernel_fallback_variant and monitor p99 latency.
  4. Create JIRA with spec_id samples and attach traces.

Metrics (must emit these; names are proposed):
- speculative.admit_count (counter)
- speculative.admit_rate (per-route; ratio of admits/request)
- speculative.wasted_tokens (counter) — tokens generated by speculation that were not used in final output
- speculative.wasted_tokens_ratio (gauge) — wasted_tokens / total_tokens
- speculative.rollback_count (counter)
- speculative.rollback_rate (gauge) — rollbacks / admits
- speculative.latency_p50/p95/p99 (histogram) — admitted vs non-admitted slices
- kernel.fallback_count (counter)
- kv.speculative_insert_count (counter)
- kv.speculative_hit_rate (gauge)
- quality.regression_{route} (gauge) — automatic eval score delta vs baseline for keyed prompt sets
- cost.speculative_compute_ms (counter) / cost.per_request

Suggested alert thresholds (example starting points):
- speculative.rollback_rate > 0.02 AND admits > 1000 in 5m => P1 review
- speculative.wasted_tokens_ratio > 0.25 for 10m => P2 investigation
- quality.regression_{critical-promptset} drop >= 2% => immediate rollback of speculation by feature flag

Canary / rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal-only synthetic traffic; collect metrics and sanity-check KV eviction and reservation failures.
- Phase 1: 1% of production requests for non-critical routes, conservative thresholds. Observe 48–72 hours.
- Phase 2: 10% production on mixed routes, enable fastpath if kernel.can_fastpath == true. Run nightly evals on golden prompt sets.
- Phase 3: ramp to 100% with automated gating (if rollback_rate < threshold AND quality regressions absent).

Experimentation and validation checklist:
- Compare latency deltas per-percentile (p50/p95/p99) between admitted vs blocked traffic.
- Track number of example prompts where final output differs semantically (manual inspection sample).
- TTL tuning: A/B two speculative KV TTL values (30s vs 5m) to measure hit/miss tradeoff.
- Kernel variant pairing: run microbench to ensure kernel.can_fastpath is predictive for p99.

Implementation checklist (engineering tasks):
- [ ] Implement Admission Controller RPC + unit tests
- [ ] Scheduler reservation APIs and per-node speculative budget enforcement
- [ ] KV tagging + invalidate-by-tag support + short TTL defaults
- [ ] Kernel probe API + probe sampling logic
- [ ] Trace & metric instrumentation (spec_id tagging)
- [ ] Rollback automation for route feature flag flip
- [ ] E2E smoke tests and chaos scenario (simulate kernel mismatch, KV eviction race)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where to compute uncertainty_score? Client-side (cheaper) or server-side (more trustworthy)? Prefer server-side for uniformity, but must be performant.
- How aggressive should per-node compute-budgets be in Dedicated mode vs Hosted? Dedicated customers may need higher caps by contract.
- Can we expose spec_id in customer logs for debugging or does that leak internal policy? Consider sanitized visibility.

Appendix: sample alert query snippets
- speculative.rollback_rate > 0.02 AND sum(admit_count) > 1000 over 5m
- rate(speculative.wasted_tokens[5m]) / sum(rate(tokens_generated[5m])) > 0.25

Notes / next steps:
- Review admission heuristics with solutions engineering for common customer workloads (LLM agents, code completion, chat).
- Ship minimal probe instrumentation behind feature flag and run internal canary for two weeks.
- Schedule follow-up doc to codify safe defaults per-customer-tier and per-hardware-class.

-- end of playbook --
